sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: This visa lets you stay in Australia while your Protection visa application is being processed.

sections.heading: Overview > You must
sections.text:
- comply with all Australian laws

Help with your visa

If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help with your visa application.

sections.heading: Overview > With this visa, you can
sections.text: - stay in Australia lawfully while your Protection visa application is being processed.

sections.heading: Overview > Processing time
sections.text: For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool. This will show the processing times for recently decided applications. It is a guide only and not specific to your application.

sections.heading: About this visa > Types of bridging visas
sections.text:
You can stay in Australia lawfully while your Protection visa application is being processed.

There are two types of BVEs:

- Bridging (General) visa (subclass 050) - generally if you are currently unlawful, the holder of a BVE 050 or the holder of a BVD 041
- Bridging (Protection Visa Applicant) visa (subclass 051) - used in limited situations. This allows certain eligible non-citizens (as specified by the Regulations) to remain lawfully in Australia while their Protection visa application is being finalised.

sections.heading: About this visa > With this visa you can
sections.text:
You may be eligible for this visa if, within 45 days of arriving in Australia, you:

- were refused immigration clearance, or
- entered Australia without immigration clearance and were identified as an unlawful non-citizen.

You must also:

- be in immigration detention
- have applied for a protection visa that is still being assessed, or have applied for judicial review of a protection visa refusal
- meet other age, health or nomination requirements, or be eligible for a further Bridging Visa E (subclass 051).

sections.heading: About this visa > How long you can stay
sections.text:
A BVE 051 will end immediately if the following situations occur:

- you leave Australia
- we grant you a substantive visa
- we grant you another Bridging visa in relation to the same matter that your current BVE is associated with
- your BVE is cancelled

In all other situations one of the following outcomes will determine when your BVE ceases:

If your Bridging visa relates to an ongoing visa application

Your BVE will cease 35 calendar days after:

- our refusal decision or a decision by the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART) (or equivalent) in relation to your associated substantive visa application
- a determination that your substantive visa application or an application for review by the ART is invalid
- you withdraw your substantive visa application or application for review by the ART

If your Bridging visa relates to ongoing judicial review

Your BVE will cease 28 calendar days after:

- the judicial review proceedings are complete
- you withdraw your judicial review application

Check your visa status in VEVO if:

- you (or the other person) have been notified of an outcome on your application or review
- you (or the other person) withdraw an application or review
- the ART or a court determines your matter should be reconsidered by the ART or Department
- you are granted another visa

sections.heading: About this visa > Stay longer
sections.text:
You cannot stay in Australia longer by extending this visa.

Explore your visa options.

sections.heading: About this visa > Include family
sections.text: You can include members of the family unit in your application when you apply.

sections.heading: About this visa > Your obligations
sections.text: You and anyone included in your application must comply with all Australian laws.

sections.heading: About this visa > Travel
sections.text: A BVE allows you to stay in Australia lawfully for a short time. It will end immediately if you leave Australia. You will not be able to return unless you have another visa.

sections.heading: About this visa > Visa label
sections.text: We will digitally link your visa to your passport. You will not get a label in your passport.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have been refused or bypassed immigration clearance
sections.text: You must have been refused immigration clearance or bypassed immigration clearance and come to our notice within 45 days, and all of the following apply to you:

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have applied for a protection visa
sections.text: You must have applied for a protection visa.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet other specific requirements
sections.text: You must meet other specific requirements relating to age, health or nomination, or you meet the requirements for a further BVE (subclass 051).

sections.heading: Eligibility > Age
sections.text: You can be any age to apply for this visa.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet health requirement
sections.text: You and any family members who apply for the visa with you may need to meet our health requirement

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet character requirement
sections.text:
You must meet our character requirement.

We might also ask that other family members meet the requirement.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply
sections.text:
Check if you already hold a BVE before you apply for this visa in VEVO.

In some cases, when you make a valid application for a substantive visa in Australia, you will also have applied for a BVE. We will tell you if this happens. In this case, you do not need to lodge a separate application.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Organise health exams before you apply
sections.text: You might need to have health examinations. You can complete them before you apply or you can wait until after you apply.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Get help with your application
sections.text:
Only some people can help you with your application. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be:

- a registered migration agent
- a legal practitioner, or
- an exempt person.

You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf about your visa matter.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents
sections.text:
Gather the documents you need for your application.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Provide accurate information
sections.text: Provide accurate information. See what happens if you cannot prove your identity or do not provide true information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Identity documents
sections.text:
Provide the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates.

Also provide:

- a national identity card, if you have one
- proof of change of name

Documents that prove a change of name include:

- a marriage or divorce certificate
- change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority
- documents that show other names you have been known by

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Character documents
sections.text: We will tell you if and when you need to get a police certificate.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Tell us you are getting help
sections.text:
To nominate someone to:

- receive your correspondence, use Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration assistance, use Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount if you applied online, or send with your paper application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa
sections.text:
The preferred method is to apply online.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Apply online
sections.text:
You and anyone included in your application must be in Australia when you lodge your BVE application.

You can apply for a BVE if you do not already have an undecided BVE application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Apply on paper
sections.text:
Complete Form 1008 Application for Bridging visa E.

Send your paper application by post to the Australian Visa and Citizenship Office nearest to you. You may need to attend an interview as part of the application process.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply
sections.text:
See what you can and must do after you apply.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > What will happen after you apply
sections.text: We will let you know when we have received your application and documents.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Status updates
sections.text:
We cannot give updates on applications within the standard processing time.

Wait for us to contact you.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Travel
sections.text:
A BVE lets you temporarily stay in Australia. It will end when you leave Australia. If you travel outside Australia after you apply, you need a visa to return.

Learn about visa expiry.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Health exams
sections.text: We will let you know if you need health examinations.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Biometrics
sections.text: We might ask for biometrics (fingerprints and photo). We will let you know if you need to provide them.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Send more information
sections.text:
Send the documents to the office where you lodged the application.

We might also ask you to provide more information.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Mistakes on your application
sections.text:
Let us know as soon as you can if you made a mistake on your application.

Complete Form 1023 Notification of incorrect answers.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Help with your application
sections.text:
Let us know if you no longer want someone to:

- receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration advice - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Send written notification or your forms to the office you submitted your application.

For more information see Who can help you with your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
Things you need to let us know about after you have applied include:

- changes to your phone number, email, address or passport
- the birth of a child
- you want to withdraw your application

See how to tell us if your situation changes.

sections.heading: Step by step > Visa outcome
sections.text:
We will tell you when we decide on your visa application.

We will let you know in writing our decision about your visa application. The letter or email will tell you:

- your visa grant number
- the date your visa starts
- your visa conditions

Keep a copy of the letter with you when in Australia.

If we refuse your visa we will let you know in writing. We will tell you:

- why it was refused
- whether you have a right to a review of the decision

New step description

sections.heading: When you have this visa > In Australia
sections.text:
What you can do when you have this visa

- stay lawfully in Australia until a decision is made on your substantive visa application

To see your specific conditions use VEVO.

What you must do on this visa (your obligations)

- comply with all Australian laws

Tell us if things change

Things you need to let us know about include:

- changes to your phone number, email, address or passport
- you want to withdraw your application

See how to let us know if there is a change in your situation.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Leaving Australia
sections.text:
Before you leave

Check your travel documents

You must have a valid passport or other travel document to leave Australia.

At the Border

Leaving the airport faster

We have an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport. You might be able to leave the airport faster if you use SmartGate.

After you leave

International Movement Record

To prove you have been to Australia, request your international movement records by completing Form 1359 Request for international movement records.
